acquisition_method: GitHub connector read of README, MATLAB source, repository metadata and recursive tree; raw pinned file downloads independently verified against Git blob SHA-1.

assertions.finding: Repository README identifies software used for the Kuchen/Becker paper and names its authors.
assertions.scope: Author-code attribution as stated by the repository; not an independent replication.

assertions.finding: README describes loading the published control supplement, then correcting it and saving separate MAT files. The MATLAB code performs those operations in that order.
assertions.scope: Stronger evidence that this generation-filtering step is downstream of the intended control XLSX. It does not certify what acquisition/export selection occurred before that file was created.

assertions.finding: The code places unscaled columns B/E and H on cycle-duration and birth-time axes labeled hours.
assertions.scope: Direct author-code support for hours in control cycle lengths and birth times. No exact clock origin, frame mapping or event-boundary convention follows. Perturbation processing is not implemented by this control loop.

assertions.finding: The control loader constructs loss endpoints from H+D and H+G; it derives maxtime from their maximum and groups endpoints within 0.01 of that maximum.
assertions.scope: This is a calculation used by the authors, not an independently logged administrative recording end. The 0.01 buffer is a numerical rule, not imaging precision or proof that every selected loss is administrative.

assertions.finding: The script uses ceil(5% of selected endpoint counts), cumulative generation counts and a final generation filter before saving corrected trees.
assertions.scope: No cutoff values were computed here; the table/prose ordering discrepancy is not resolved. Do not run this future-informed filter to choose a prospective roster.

assertions.finding: Although a comment calls the window 10 hours, the actual birth-time predicate spans center−10 to center+10.
assertions.scope: Static interpretation gives a 20-hour full window. This note avoids reproducing the comment as a distinct 10-hour full-width procedure; no drift calculation was executed.

assertions.finding: The same script includes later birth-position and spatial-confound analysis after loading corrected trees.
assertions.scope: Retain the authors’ existing context analyses as prior work; this code is not an acquisition or observation-gap specification.

earlier_evidence_preserved.clarification: Earlier bounded search did not find code; this later addendum now supplies it rather than rewriting that historical search outcome.

updated_claims.K01: Control birth and cycle fields now directly mapped to hours by author code; other timing limits remain.
updated_claims.K14: Post-loading control generation filtering is now source-code-supported; export inclusion still unverified.
updated_claims.K22: Author analysis code now located; no original acquisition/export generator or full tracking dictionary identified.

limits: No author code was executed; no original or corrected dataset outcomes calculated.
The original-named control XLSX is referenced by basename, not cryptographic input hash; this inspection does not prove byte identity with every archived file version.
No exact event landmark, clock origin, continuous-observation rule or loss-reason code is established.
Current loop handles three controls; its comment says perturbations need adaptation, so no rapamycin-label resolution follows.
No repository-wide LICENSE or COPYING file was observed in the pinned recursive tree. Code snapshots remain local and excluded; no full-source redistribution claim is made.
No author contact, external submission, code adoption or execution.
